chunks: Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani and Sama'ah narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
He was asked about a man who carries goods for the people of the market, and they have assigned a price to them for him. Then they say: Sell, and whatever extra you obtain is yours.
He said: "There is no harm in that, but he should not sell to them as murabaha."

key_terms.أَهْلِ السُّوقِ: the people of the marketplace who own or consign the goods
key_terms.ازْدَدْتَ: what you gain in excess above the set amount
key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: goods or merchandise being carried and sold
key_terms.بِعْ: sell; an instruction to conduct the sale
key_terms.قِيمَةً: an assigned value or set price
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: a sale structured as murabaha, i.e. a cost-plus profit sale

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods for someone else and keep whatever exceeds the set price?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on selling goods on behalf of market people when they set a base value and allow the seller to keep any excess above it. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام permits this arrangement, while prohibiting conducting it in the form of murabaha.
